from solution import common_element


def test_issue_example_from_issue():
    """Example: [1,2,3,4,5] and [5,6,7,8,9] share 5 so returns True."""
    # common = {5}, non-empty => True
    assert common_element([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], [5, 6, 7, 8, 9]) == True


def test_issue_common_at_different_positions():
    """Returns True if they have at least one common element at different indexes."""
    # common = {1}, non-empty => True
    assert common_element([1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 1]) == True


def test_issue_common_only_last_element():
    """Returns True if the only common element is at the end of both lists."""
    # common = {5}, non-empty => True
    assert common_element([1, 2, 5], [6, 7, 5]) == True


def test_issue_disjoint_same_length():
    """Returns False when lists of same length have no common element."""
    # common = {}, empty => False
    assert common_element([1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]) == False


def test_issue_identical_lists():
    """Returns True if identical lists have at least one common element."""
    # common = {1, 2}, non-empty => True
    assert common_element([1, 2], [1, 2]) == True


def test_issue_single_element_common():
    """Returns True if single-element lists share that element."""
    # common = {1}, non-empty => True
    assert common_element([1], [1]) == True


def test_issue_single_element_disjoint():
    """Returns False if single-element lists share no element."""
    # common = {}, empty => False
    assert common_element([1], [2]) == False


def test_issue_first_empty():
    """Returns False if the first list is empty so no common element exists."""
    # common = {}, empty => False
    assert common_element([], [1, 2, 3]) == False


def test_issue_second_empty():
    """Returns False if the second list is empty so no common element exists."""
    # common = {}, empty => False
    assert common_element([1, 2, 3], []) == False


def test_issue_both_empty():
    """Returns False if both lists are empty so no common element exists."""
    # common = {}, empty => False
    assert common_element([], []) == False


def test_contract_returns_true_exactly():
    """Returns True if they have at least one common element."""
    # common = {2}, non-empty => True
    assert common_element([1, 2], [2, 3]) is True


def test_contract_returns_false_exactly():
    """Returns False if they have no common element."""
    # common = {}, empty => False
    assert common_element([1, 2], [3, 4]) is False
